posts.text: If your wallet is small and it’s still not growing, read this. You don’t need bigger trades. You need better risk management. Let’s say you have a $200 wallet. Before entering any trade, decide one thing first: “How much am I okay losing if this trade is wrong?” For example, fix your maximum risk at $5 per trade. Now don’t randomly put $5 as margin and choose 20x leverage. That’s not how it works. First find your entry, then find the technical stop-loss the level where your trade idea becomes invalid. Suppose your SL is 5% away. Maximum risk = $5 SL distance = 5% Position size = $5 ÷ 5% = $100 Only after this calculate the leverage according to the margin you want to use. If you use $10 margin: $100 ÷ $10 = 10x leverage So if the 5% SL gets hit, your planned loss is around $5, not your whole account. posts.text: CAN THESE CRAZY BULL RUN TARGETS REALLY HAPPEN? Bull markets can push prices far beyond expectations, but market cap matters more than hype. $BTC at $195K, $ETH at $14.6K, and BNB above $3K are aggressive but still within the realm of a powerful bull cycle. $SOL at $2,300+ and HYPE near $859 would require extremely large capital inflows. But PENGU at $10+ and PUMP above $7 would need valuations in the hundreds of billions to trillions — making those targets far more difficult under current token supply. The mistake many traders make is looking only at price. Always calculate: Target Price × Circulating Supply = Required Market Cap In a bull run, anything can pump hard but tokenomics and market cap tell you whether the target actually makes sense.

posts.text: $XAU time for sell, open big short now and make money with me entry 4135-4165 sl 4180 tp 4099-4050 Short $XAU 👇 {future}(XAUUSDT) Why did $XAU and $BTC sell off together on Oct 7? On the surface, these two markets look completely unrelated. But underneath, they can react to the same macro pressure. A stronger USD, rising US yields, and Brent pushing above $100 all mean tighter financial conditions and less risk appetite. Gold gets pressured because it doesn’t generate yield. Bitcoin gets pressured because it’s still trading more like a risk asset, with leverage making the move even sharper. Bottom line: when yields and the USD rise together, the market is repricing the real cost of capital and the possibility that the Fed stays restrictive for longer.

posts.text: The Bitcoin Policy Institute said it has changed its name to the Finney Foundation for Open Technology and announced its first group of fellows. Their areas of focus include free speech; governance and emerging technologies; economics; national security; AI and democracy; space and industrial policy; Bitcoin and law; machine learning and health; and biotechnology.

posts.text: According to ChainCatcher citing The Globe and Mail, Canada's S&P/TSX Composite fell 2.1% on November 18, dropping 737.25 points to 34,578.05, its largest one-day decline in nearly five months and lowest close since June 10. The index fell more than major U.S. benchmarks and closed at its lowest level since June. It has declined more than 6% from its August record high as metal and energy stocks sold off; companies in those sectors account for about one-third of the benchmark's weighting. The materials sector fell 5.4%, with Agnico Eagle Mines down 6.3%. Gold fell 3.4% to a 14-month low, while copper dropped 5.25%, its steepest percentage decline in 19 months. U.S. crude futures settled 3.2% lower at $83.26 a barrel. The energy and financial sectors fell 3.8% and 2.2%, respectively.

posts.text: Peapods Finance said it has contained selling pressure on PEAS and is conducting a post-incident review while attempting to recover funds taken by the attacker. According to Foresight News, the incident involved PEAS being minted on an L2, bridged to mainnet, and sold; the team’s preliminary assessment is that the deployer’s private key may have been compromised. The key was used to set minting permissions on the L2 and mint tokens. The team has removed 98-99% of liquidity on the L2 to limit further withdrawals by the attacker. PEAS cannot be minted on mainnet, and only liquidity already on the bridge can be withdrawn. The team advised users to temporarily remove all on-chain LP and LVF positions.

posts.text: According to ChainCatcher, OpenAI President Greg Brockman said the company’s cybersecurity business will eventually surpass its coding business. He said he is currently in “full management mode,” overseeing day-to-day operations and prioritizing enterprise customers and cybersecurity. Cybersecurity is already an important, fast-growing revenue source for OpenAI, though Brockman did not disclose figures. OpenAI has launched a dedicated cybersecurity model and a red-teaming agent, and its Daybreak project provides tools to businesses, governments, and security professionals. Thibault Sottiaux, who leads OpenAI’s product and platform teams, said Brockman took part in the decision to delay a model that did not meet safety standards. Sottiaux also said Brockman authorized pausing about a quarter of product work for several weeks to reassign engineers to internal security infrastructure.

posts.text: According to ChainCatcher citing WIRED, Nvidia interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress used the phrase “We’ve got this” publicly three times in 24 hours, according to a Nov. 18 report. On Tuesday’s third-quarter earnings call, she said the company’s momentum was real, demand was accelerating and supply continued to grow, adding that customers, partners and employees stood with Nvidia. Kress repeated the phrase at a company town hall on Wednesday, saying Nvidia’s innovation ambitions and commitments to customers, partners and shareholders would not change. She likened employees to a crowd singing together at a University of Florida football game. Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones had previously said the board had no intention of reinstating Jensen Huang.

posts.text: According to Jin10, Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said Thursday that consumption is expected to recover after a brief slowdown. He added that the decline in private spending in third-quarter GDP data was within the central bank’s expectations. Speaking in parliament, Ueda said nominal wages would rise steadily while inflation slows gradually, and that higher household income would support consumption. He said consumption remained resilient overall and that the third-quarter decline was mainly due to rising living costs and adverse weather. “We expect consumption to return to a moderate growth trend,” he said. The comments suggest that weak third-quarter consumption alone will not prevent the Bank of Japan from raising rates again in the near term.

posts.text: The National Cybersecurity Notification Center issued an alert about a high-risk Java remote code execution vulnerability. According to Odaily, overseas security research organization Calif disclosed the Java4Shell vulnerability, CVE-2026-114938, on November 17. The flaw lies in the Open JDK Base 64 decoding path; submitting specially crafted Base 64 data to a Java application can trigger an out-of-bounds write to heap memory, potentially exposing sensitive information or enabling remote code execution. Oracle has released an emergency fix. The vulnerability affects a wide range of applications, and many Java applications exposed to the internet may be targeted in cyberattacks.

posts.text: The administration of U.S. President Donald Trump has launched a Threat Disruption Center to disrupt money flows to foreign criminal networks involved in scams, cybercrime and sextortion. According to Cointelegraph, the Homeland Security Task Force’s National Coordination Center announced the unit’s launch on Wednesday. posts.text: Ethereum developer ilitteri has submitted an EIP draft proposing native support for the hash-based post-quantum signature scheme LeanSPHINCS in frame transactions. According to Foresight News, the proposal would add the scheme to frame transactions defined by EIP-8141. Under the draft, transactions would use a dedicated validation frame to specify required signatures, with signature data kept separate from the transaction itself but propagated with it through the mempool and included in the same block. Nodes would verify the signatures before executing transactions. The proposal remains in draft form, has not been assigned an official EIP number, and requires a more complete technical specification.

posts.text: Ethereum Foundation developer Marius van der Wijden said at a developers’ meeting on Monday that the upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade could affect up to 15,000 automated contracts, with assets worth hundreds of thousands of dollars estimated to be at risk. According to Odaily, the issues center on proposals EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, which would change fees for storing and reading data on Ethereum and could create compatibility problems for existing contracts as gas costs change. Security auditor ChainSecurity identified 152 issues, about half of which overlapped with the foundation’s internal research. Dedaub reviewed about 25,000 contracts and found 70 additional medium- to high-risk issues, including 22 not previously identified by the foundation. posts.text: According to ChainCatcher, Grvt has launched Stable Funding Perps, a product of its hybrid decentralized exchange built on an Ethereum Layer 2 network using ZKsync. The RWA-linked perpetual contracts initially cover seven commodity markets, with funding fees settled in USDC at market close from Monday to Friday. The contracts use a request-for-quote model, with market makers providing real-time bids and asks and managing hedges in traditional financial markets. Grvt charges no trading fees, incorporating execution costs into quotes. Funding rates differ for long and short positions and may adjust for weekend and holiday financing conditions. The product initially has a high minimum trade size. According to Foresight News, Stables offers collection, currency conversion, and cross-border payment services designed to address intermediary costs and settlement delays. Stables connects local banks and payment systems to USDT settlement through a single API. Its infrastructure covers more than 160 markets and processes more than $2 billion in USDT transactions annually. In May 2026, Stables integrated USDT0 into its developer platform, enabling businesses to transfer USDT across multiple blockchain networks without managing bridges themselves. posts.text: Blockstream and French technology group Thales have launched an institutional Bitcoin custody system that keeps keys offline. According to Odaily, Bitcoin News said on X that Blockstream’s Secure-MPC divides signing authority into multiple shares, none of which can transfer funds on its own. The signing protocol runs entirely within a Thales hardware security module, and the keys and shares never leave the hardware. The system is designed for custody banks and prime brokers. Adam Back advocated simpler offline security measures to address AI-assisted cyberattacks.

Options traders are pricing in a 7% stock reaction after Tuesday’s earnings report, the largest implied move ahead of an Nvidia report since February 2025 and above the median move of 3.2% over the past eight quarters. posts.text: Former New York Fed President William C. Dudley said the Fed’s effort to reduce inflation without harming employment may not succeed. According to Odaily, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has repeatedly stressed the 2% inflation target, but policy tightening has remained limited and inflation expectations have not fully stabilized. Dudley described the approach as “pain-free disinflation,” relying on the Fed’s credibility to anchor expectations and gradually lower inflation without a significant impact on employment. He said similar policies in recent years failed to bring inflation back to target. Dudley said that if the Fed continues to rely on statements without taking sufficient action, inflation expectations could move closer to actual inflation, making price stability harder to achieve.

posts.text: According to ChainCatcher, Real Vision Co-Founder and CEO Raoul Pal said at Solana Breakpoint that the financial system would gradually move onto blockchain and that financial markets were moving toward tokenization. He cited Solana’s real-world asset market, which grew from $10 million to $2 billion over 14 to 15 months, as evidence of the trend. Pal said he had discussed the shift as early as 2014 and that it was now beginning to take shape. Pal said AI agents could become economic participants and drive more on-chain activity, helping support a potential $100 trillion scale by 2034 to 2035. He added that wider use of blockspace and the development of economically significant infrastructure and businesses on-chain could change how GDP is calculated, arguing that blockchain’s potential market and economic impact extend beyond its role as revenue-generating infrastructure or a tool.

posts.text: Bitcoin’s Ahr999 indicator stood at 0.31 on November 17, below the 0.45 level it uses to mark an accumulation zone, according to CoinGlass data. It dropped below 0.45 on November 6 and has stayed there for 11 straight days.The 200-day average cost of buying bitcoin through dollar-cost averaging (DCA), where an investor buys a fixed amount at regular intervals, is $72,400. With bitcoin trading near $64,500, the price is about 11% below that cost.The last time the indicator was below 0.45, from May 29 to August 19 this year, the window lasted about 82 days. Over bitcoin’s history, Ahr999 has spent a total of 741 days below 0.45.The Ahr999 indicator is designed to help DCA investors time their purchases. It combines two things: how bitcoin’s price compares with its 200-day DCA cost, and how far the price sits from a long-term growth estimate.
